Not every RCA capture is usable, and that cuts the other way too: a same-day (2026-08-14) capture of a different current-site page (ForConsumers/NaturalGas.aspx) IS a DataDome JS-challenge shell (403, ~2.4KB) -- captures on this domain are page/timestamp-dependent, so neither 'no snapshots exist' nor 'everything is a JS shell' is accurate. Alaska DNR (dog.dnr.alaska.gov) is NOT blocked -- the prior note's '403 behind a DataDome bot-challenge' claim was false. Reproduced live 2026-09-15: the site root and /Services/Pipelines both return HTTP 200 with real content; only the guessed singular path /Services/Pipeline (no trailing pipeline name) 404s -- a bad URL, not a block. ACCESS CORRECTION (2026-09-15 re-audit): the prior pass's blocked-source claims were partly false and are restated here. rca.alaska.gov LIVE genuinely 403s: reproduced with curl (browser UA, --compressed) -> HTTP 403, 'Server: DataDome' / 'X-DataDome: protected', 773-byte challenge page. But Wayback is NOT empty for this host -- the prior claim of 'zero snapshots' was false: CDX lists thousands of captures back to 2004. The 2026-08-14 capture of the site root (web.archive.org/web/20260814171212/https://rca.alaska.gov/) redirects to the pre-2020 RCAWeb/home.aspx template and returns real page content (menus, docket/meeting links), not a JS shell. A 2005 capture of rca.alaska.gov/data/companyDetail.html?acronym=ENSTAR (200, real content) is an actual RCA 'Company: ENSTAR' record: CPCN #4 ('ENSTAR NATURAL GAS COMPANY, A DIVISION OF SEMCO', Gas) plus a docket history including U-01-007 'ALASKA PIPELINE COMPANY AND UNION OIL COMPANY OF CALIFORNIA, GAS SALES AGMT' (2001) and U-00-088 'ENSTAR NATURAL GAS CO. & ALASKA PIPELINE CO., INVE[STIGATION]' (2000) -- independent state-regulator confirmation of the APC/ENSTAR relationship already established via the SEC 10-K. It is a company/docket index, though, not a segment record: no mileage, diameter, capacity, pressure, or construction/proposal/start date for any specific segment, and it does not name 'Anchorage System.' Not every RCA capture is usable, and that cuts the other way too: a same-day (2026-08-14) capture of a different current-site page (ForConsumers/NaturalGas.aspx) IS a DataDome JS-challenge shell (403, ~2.4KB) -- captures on this domain are page/timestamp-dependent, so neither 'no snapshots exist' nor 'everything is a JS shell' is accurate. A direct lookup of ENSTAR's own certificate detail page (data/certificateDetail.html?CPCN=4, the record most likely to carry system extent) returns Wayback 404 -- genuinely not archived, not a block.

resolutions.researcher_notes: ADJUDICATED: P0146 (Alaska Pipeline Project) and P0174 (Denali - The Alaska Gas Pipeline) are TWO GENUINELY COMPETING PROPOSALS, not one physical project entered twice. Two independent origins say so explicitly. (1) Office of the Federal Coordinator, arcticgas.gov: 'Denali-The Alaska Gas Pipeline, a joint venture of North Slope producers ConocoPhillips and BP, was established in April 2008 TO COMPETE WITH the TransCanada project ... In May 2011, Denali announced it would no longer pursue development.' (2) CRS R40963: 'the State of Alaska's 2008 award to TransCanada ... and the concurrent announcement of a COMPETING pipeline proposal, the Denali project, by BP and ConocoPhillips. Through 2010, the Denali and TransCanada pipelines were proceeding along similar tracks. However, in May 2011, Denali's developers announced the discontinuation of their pipeline project'. They differ on every axis that identifies a project: SPONSORS (TransCanada + ExxonMobil vs BP + ConocoPhillips); REGULATORY VEHICLE (AGIA license awarded Dec 2008 + FERC pre-file Docket PF09-11-000 vs a non-AGIA proposal with its own separate FERC pre-file); CAPACITY as proposed (CRS: TransCanada 4.5-5.0 Bcf/d; Denali 4.0 Bcf/d); SCOPE (Denali always included its own gas treatment plant, the AGIA project initially did not); and END DATE (Denali withdrew May 2011; APP's prefile docket was terminated 26 Aug 2014). They shared an origin (Prudhoe Bay), a corridor (the Alaska Highway route to Alberta) and a rough design scale, which is why the rows look alike. Both are re-pointed to APP-specific sources in fills[]. A second-order concern for P0174 (raised as a cross-row lead, not edited here): CRS states Denali was a 4.0 Bcf/d proposal, while GEM carries 4,500 MMcf/d on that row, so the identical capacity that prompted the duplicate suspicion may itself be an artifact of the same misattribution.

resolutions.recommendation: no merge - keep P0147, P0293 and P6534 as separate rows; record P6534 as an AKLNG component and P0293 as the abandoned rival in-state plan
resolutions.researcher_notes: DUPLICATE ADJUDICATION for the Alaska cluster, which the brief flags as easy to conflate. (1) P6534 Point Thomson Unit Gas Transmission Pipeline (63 mi, 32-inch, 865 MMcf/d) IS part of the same FERC application but is NOT a duplicate of P0147 - it is a physically distinct feeder line. The FERC order authorises, as separate facilities, '62.5 miles of 32-inch-diameter pipeline on the North Slope, which will [run] from the Point Thomson Unit gas production facility to the Prudhoe Bay Treatment Plant (Point Thomson Unit Gas Transmission Line)' and '1.0 miles of 60-inch-diameter pipeline ... (Prudhoe Bay Unit Gas Transmission Line)', alongside the 806.9-mile Mainline. Resource Report No. 1 gives the Point Thomson line its own specs - 62.5 mi, 32-inch, 865 MMSCF/D average stream day rate, 920 MMSCF/D peak, MAOP 1,150 psig - which match P6534's sheet values exactly, so P6534 is correctly and independently recorded. The relationship should be NAMED (P6534 is AKLNG's Point Thomson lateral; Glenfarne's Phase One 'may also include the 63-mile, 32-inch Point Thomson Lateral Pipeline'), and P0147's 807 mi must stay Mainline-only so the two rows do not double-count. Note also that the 60-inch, 1-mile Prudhoe Bay Unit line appears to have no GEM row at all. (2) P0293 Alaska Stand Alone Pipeline (ASAP) is NOT the same project as P0147 and has not been folded into AKLNG Phase One, despite sharing a sponsor (AGDC), a corridor and a North-Slope-to-Southcentral purpose. EIA's Historical Projects sheet keeps ASAP as its own row with different physical specs - 737 mi, '12,36' inch, 500 MMcf/d, $9,970M, status 'On Hold' - and describes it as 'a buried in-state natural gas pipeline ... considered to be the backup plan to the Alaska LNG project', terminating at 'the ENSTAR system near Point Mackenzie in the Mat-Su Valley', not Nikiski. AKLNG Phase One is a 739-mile 42-inch line under FERC docket CP17-178 held by 8 Star Alaska LLC; ASAP is a separate, dormant state project. Different diameter, different capacity, different terminus, different authorisation - two rows, correctly. (3) P0146 Alaska Pipeline Project (TransCanada/ExxonMobil, FERC PF09-11) and P0174 Denali (BP/ConocoPhillips, FERC PF08-26) are 1,126-1,700 mile Alaska Highway export lines to Alberta from an earlier era, already adjudicated as distinct in their own shards; nothing in AKLNG's record folds either into P0147, and I have not merged anything.

resolutions.recommendation: Keep P0174 and P0146 as SEPARATE rows - do not merge; they are rival consortia, not one project
resolutions.researcher_notes: ADJUDICATION of the P0174-vs-P0146 duplicate hypothesis raised by the orchestrator: they are NOT the same project. They are the two genuinely competing 2000s-era Alaska Highway proposals, and the evidence is regulatory, not inferential. (1) SEPARATE FERC DOCKETS, described side by side in separate sections of the SAME document: FERC's ANGTA Eleventh Report to Congress (Feb 2011) has 'B. Denali's Proposal ... Denali plans to construct and operate a gas treatment plant (GTP) near Prudhoe Bay and a 48-inch-diameter pipeline to transport up to 4.5 Bcf/d from the Alaska North Slope to the Alberta Hub ... Docket No. PF08-26-000' and, immediately following, 'C. TC Alaska's Proposal ... Docket No. PF09-11-000'. A regulator does not open two pre-filing dockets for one project. (2) SEPARATE SPONSORS: Denali = BP plc + ConocoPhillips (50/50 JV incorporated as Denali - The Alaska Gas Pipeline LLC, announced 2008-04-08); the Alaska Pipeline Project = TransCanada/TC Energy + ExxonMobil, built on TransCanada's 2008 AGIA licence from the State of Alaska. Denali's own filing acknowledges TransCanada's separate AGIA licence. (3) SEPARATE OPEN SEASONS, months apart: TC Alaska's closed 2010-07-30, Denali's closed 2010-10-04. (4) SEPARATE ENDINGS: Denali withdrew from pre-filing 2011-05-17 (ANGTA Twelfth Report); the APP continued and is recorded on P0146 as cancelled in 2014. (5) DIFFERENT PHYSICAL SCOPE: the ANGTA Twelfth Report describes the APP as 'a gas treatment plant (GTP) near Prudhoe Bay, about 58 miles of 32-inch-diameter pipeline from the processing plant at the Point Thomson Field to the GTP, and about 745 miles of 48-inch-diameter mainline pipeline from the GTP to the Alaska-Yukon border', versus Denali's 730-mile Alaska Mainline + 1,020-mile Canada Mainline to Blueberry Hill, AB. (6) The trade press treats them as rivals throughout: AP (2010-04-07) frames Denali's open season against the competing TransCanada/Exxon project, and NGI (2011-05-23) quotes TransCanada VP Tony Palmer on Denali - 'They're an independent project'. The shared 4,500 MMcf/d is not a duplication artefact but the consequence of both consortia sizing to the same contracted ANS gas volume, and each states it in its own documents. CAVEAT recorded rather than a clean confirmation: the two rows share a corridor (both follow the Alaska Highway from a Prudhoe Bay GTP) and a capacity, so a future reviewer will ask this question again - the answer belongs in ResearcherNotes on both rows. Separately, P0146's LengthKnown=1700.00 is labelled 'km' while every source for that project says 1,700 MILES; that is a defect on P0146, flagged in cross_row_leads, not a reason to merge.

resolutions.recommendation: no edit needed; add the cross-border scope + flow-reversal context to ResearcherNotes
resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, operating interstate gas transmission pipeline, corroborated across CER (Canada Energy Regulator pipeline profile, apps.cer-rec.gc.ca, section updated Oct 2024), Enbridge's own 'Energy Infrastructure Assets' factsheet PDF, the operator's mnpp.com/US site + FAQ page, offshore-technology.com (GlobalData market-data page), and three Federal Register / PHMSA documents (1996 FERC NOI, 1996 FERC order notice, 2006 PHMSA waiver-request notice). PipelineType=transmission confirmed independently by mnpp.com ('684-mile transmission pipeline system') and offshore-technology.com ('owns and operates transmission pipeline system'). No duplicate risk: no other PID in the US gas roster covers this system. CAVEAT 1 -- CROSS-BORDER SCOPE (orchestrator framing correction): the task brief characterized this row as 'the US portion' of a cross-border system. That is NOT what the sheet records: GEM's own StartLocation/StartCountryOrArea = Goldboro, Nova Scotia, Canada and EndLocation/EndCountryOrArea = Dracut, Massachusetts, United States (confirmed via the live GEM CSV, sheet row 70), and LengthKnown=1432 km / Capacity=830 MMcf/d are WHOLE-SYSTEM figures (Enbridge's factsheet states the identical 1,432 km / '889 miles' total, split as US 552 km + Canada 880 km). So P0212 is the ENTIRE binational M&NP system in one row, not a US-only segment -- there is no companion Canada-only PID on this roster. This is not a data defect (the recorded endpoints and totals are internally consistent and well-sourced), just a correction to how the row should be read; every fill below states explicitly which country/segment each individual source describes so a reviewer is never left assuming a Canada-only or US-only figure covers the whole row. CAVEAT 2 -- FLOW REVERSAL: CER states offshore Nova Scotia gas (ExxonMobil's Sable Offshore Energy Project from late 1999, Encana's Deep Panuke from 2013) supplied the line until production ended in 2018; 'Since 2019, the Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline (M&NP) transports natural gas imported from the U.S. Production may include U.S. basins such as Appalachia or Canada's W[estern Canada]' -- i.e. the physical flow direction reversed (now south-to-north into the Maritimes) even though the pipeline's physical start/end points are unchanged, consistent with mnpp.com/US's own statement that flow 'currently...from south to north as the offshore Nova Scotia gas supply is permanently shut-in.' Per the brief's specific guidance for this row, the start location (Goldboro) is NOT moved despite the reversal -- confirmed correct as recorded. CAVEAT 3 -- minor scope-defined length discrepancy: mnpp.com/US states a '684-mile transmission pipeline system' total, while Enbridge's factsheet states 889 miles (1,432 km) total -- exactly matching the sheet's recorded 1432 km. mnpp.com separately describes a jointly-owned 101-mile 'Joint Facilities' segment (co-owned with Portland Natural Gas Transmission System) and a separate Methuen-to-Beverly MA extension, which are plausibly excluded from the 684-mile figure but included in Enbridge's 889-mile system total; this is treated as a definitional-scope difference, not a material conflict, because the more precise Enbridge figure is independently corroborated component-by-component (CER: Canada-only 878-880 km; offshore-technology.com: US-only 552 km; 878+552=1430, within rounding of 1432). CAPACITY: no source states '830' literally (checked via full-text grep of the Enbridge factsheet PDF); Enbridge states 'approximately 0.8 Bcf/d' aggregate (US 0.8 Bcf/d + Canada 0.5 Bcf/d, which are NOT simply additive since Canada's throughput is now bidirectional/reduced post-2018) -- 830 MMcf/d is within rounding of 0.8 Bcf/d and is treated as REFS_ADDED at medium tier per rule 7 (agreement within rounding), not a material spec concern.

resolutions.researcher_notes: IDENTITY / DUPLICATE ADJUDICATION - the headline question for this row. Conclusion: ASAP (P0293) is NOT a duplicate of Alaska LNG (P0147), and it has NOT been folded into AKLNG's Phase 1. It is also distinct from P0146 Alaska Pipeline Project and P0174 Denali. Evidence: (1) SPONSOR'S OWN WORDS - AGDC senior VP Frank Richards, quoted by Oil & Gas Journal and KTUU in June 2018: 'AGDC is advancing two [Alaska North Slope] gas pipeline projects on parallel paths but only one will be built'; the two 'share a common mainline alignment for more than 80% of the route' but AKLNG adds liquefaction and export. Mutual exclusivity plus a shared corridor is a redundancy relationship, not one project entered twice. (2) SEPARATE REGULATORY TRACKS - ASAP is permitted by the US Army Corps of Engineers under CWA s404 / RHA s10 (NOIs 2009 and 2014, Final SEIS 22 Jun 2018) and holds Alaska DNR right-of-way lease ADL 418997; AKLNG is a FERC project. Two dockets, two lead agencies, two sets of permits. (3) DIFFERENT PHYSICAL PROJECTS - ASAP: 737 mi, 36-inch mainline + 12-inch/29-30 mi Fairbanks lateral, 1,480 psig, 500 MMcf/d, in-state delivery into ENSTAR at Point MacKenzie. AKLNG's pipeline: 42-inch, ~3,500 MMcf/d, to a Nikiski liquefaction plant. Same corridor, different pipe. (4) STILL SEPARATE TODAY - AGDC's ASAP page (current): 'the corporation is primarily focused on the Alaska LNG Project. ASAP remains as the State's back up project'; AGDC's FY2026 Capital AFE (June 2025): ASAP 'was idled following the completion of major permitting and is not currently active', while Phase 1 FEED work proceeds under the AKLNG banner. ASAP was left dormant as the state's fallback, not absorbed. (5) Against P0146/P0174: those are the 2008-2012 Alaska Gasline Inducement Act-era EXPORT trunk proposals to Alberta by TransCanada/ExxonMobil and BP/ConocoPhillips respectively - different sponsors, different destinations, both cancelled; the P0146 shard already adjudicated those two as genuinely competing proposals rather than one project. No DUPLICATE flag is raised. The caveat is bookkeeping only: any Alaska North Slope capacity/length total that adds P0293 and P0147 together is double-counting a corridor that can only be built once.

resolutions.recommendation: keep as operating/transmission; treat 'Equitrans Mainline' as the FERC-regulated Equitrans, L.P. transmission-and-storage backbone in northern West Virginia / southwestern Pennsylvania, not a single discrete pipe
resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION confirmed independently of GEM. Equitrans, L.P.'s FERC-regulated interstate transmission-and-storage system ('the mainline Equitrans, L.P. system') is documented in Equitrans Midstream Corp's FY2023 10-K (SEC EDGAR, CIK 1747009, filed 2024-02-20) and in EQT Corporation's FY2025 10-K (SEC EDGAR, CIK 33213, filed 2026-02-18, post the 2024-07-22 Equitrans Midstream Merger) as ~940-950 miles of FERC-regulated interstate pipeline with interconnects to seven interstate pipelines, in northern WV / southwestern PA / southeastern OH. The company's own FERC open-season exhibit (Equitrans, L.P., Docket CP22- (OVCX), Exhibit Z-3, 'Equitrans 2021 System Expansion', April 2021 non-binding notice, archived via Wayback since ovcx.info is now unreachable) repeatedly names the 'Equitrans Mainline System' by that exact name and describes it as overlaying 'the heart of the Marcellus and Utica shale in north central West Virginia, southwestern Pennsylvania, and eastern Ohio' -- this independently corroborates existence, classification (transmission, not gathering), and FuelSource. CAVEAT: the row's segment_name 'Equitrans Mainline' with both endpoints blank functions, in company usage, as shorthand for the whole backbone system (which is fed by laterals including the Ohio Valley Connector (P6897) and Sunrise Transmission System) rather than one bounded pipe segment -- see the companion spec concern below on Capacity for the resulting system-vs-segment conflation shared with P6896/P6897.

resolutions.recommendation: flag Capacity as a SYSTEM-level aggregate, not a segment rating, and update it to EQT's freshest disclosed figure (5,000 MMcf/d as of 2025-12-31) rather than the stale 2019-2022 figure of 4,400; the identical 4,400 MMcf/d figure is also carried on P6896 (Allegheny Valley Connector) and P6897 (Ohio Valley Connector), both individual laterals feeding INTO this system with their own much smaller true capacities
resolutions.researcher_notes: ORCHESTRATOR HEADLINE FINDING. The 4,400 MMcf/d recorded for P6895 (and identically for P6896 and P6897) is Equitrans' company-wide TOTAL THROUGHPUT CAPACITY for its entire transmission-and-storage system, not a rating of any single pipe or segment. Confirmed verbatim, word-for-word, across THREE separate company disclosures spanning three years: (1) Equitrans Midstream's OVCX Exhibit Z-3 (FERC Docket CP22-, filed 2021, 'About Equitrans Midstream Corporation' boilerplate) states, for both its April 2021 non-binding notice (YE2019 data) and June 2021 binding notice (YE2020 data): 'ETRN's transmission and storage system includes approximately 950 miles of FERC-regulated interstate pipelines... total throughput capacity of approximately 4.4 Bcf per day.' (2) The company's own transmission.html investor page (Wayback capture dated 2026-01-13, content dated 'As of December 31, 2022') restates it unchanged: 'the transmission and storage system included approximately 940 miles of FERC-regulated, interstate pipelines... with total throughput capacity of approximately 4.4 Bcf per day.' So the SAME 4.4 Bcf/d (=4,400 MMcf/d) figure for the WHOLE ~940-950 mile system was disclosed unchanged from 2019 through 2022 -- explaining why it landed identically on all three GEM rows that trace to this system. (3) It has since changed: EQT Corporation's FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-18, post the 2024-07-22 Equitrans Midstream Merger) gives a fresh 'as of December 31, 2025' system table for the same Transmission segment: 'Pipeline miles 950 / Throughput capacity (Bcf per day) 5.0 / Interconnect points 8 / Compression units 45 / Compression horsepower 197,000' -- i.e. the true CURRENT system aggregate is now 5.0 Bcf/d (5,000 MMcf/d), not 4.4 Bcf/d. So the recorded 4,400 is both (a) a system aggregate improperly applied to what reads as a segment row, and (b) stale by roughly four years. Independent cross-check: EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset (May 2018 release, 'Historical Projects' sheet, Excel row 13) records the Ohio Valley Connector itself (docket CP15-41, completed 2016-10, WV->OH, 50 mi, 30/24-inch) at its OWN additional capacity of 850 MMcf/d -- an order of magnitude below 4,400 -- which independently proves at least P6897 cannot legitimately carry the system figure. All three company documents above are Equitrans/EQT-family disclosures (one origin per the tier-discipline rule), so this is staged at tier medium / independent:false despite three separate documents/years -- an independent (non-Equitrand-family) confirmation of the CURRENT 5.0 Bcf/d figure was not found this session (WebSearch budget exhausted; only SEC EDGAR, local EIA CSVs and Wayback were reachable). Recommend the orchestrator treat P6895 as the row closest to representing this system aggregate (if any of the three should retain a system-level number, it is this one), while P6896 and P6897 should be re-sourced to their own segment-specific capacities (see cross_row_leads).

resolutions.researcher_notes: Compared against P4454 (Ohio Valley Connector Expansion Project / OVCX, FERC docket CP22-44; read that already-complete shard in full for cross-reference, not edited, per scope). In general, it parallels the Dalton Highway, from PS 1 to PS 4,' immediately followed by 'Diameter: 10 inches from PS 01 to MP 34 (34 miles); 8 inches from MP 34 to PS 04 (115 miles) / Length: 149 miles / Pressure: maximum design pressure of 1,440 psi (MAOP)'; and (2) a peer-reviewed engineering paper, Alto & McDevitt, 'Performance of the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System Fuel Gas Supply Pipeline' (Arctic Institute of North America / Univ. of Calgary Canadian Permafrost Conference proceedings, pubs.aina.ucalgary.ca), whose entire subject is this specific line: 'a gas pipeline which supplies natural gas to the four northern-most pump stations... extends south from Prudhoe Bay to Pump Station Four a distance of approximately 238 kilometers [=147.9 mi]... grades from 25.4 cm [10 in] to 20.3 cm [8 in]... commissioned in June of 1977.' Both documents are read to exhaustion below (fills[] for every column). PipelineType 'transmission' is also supported: the CPC paper states the line was designed to the requirements of 49 CFR Part 192 ('Transportation of Natural and Other Gas by Pipeline') and ASME B31.8 'Gas Transmission and Distribution Piping Systems' -- a captive, high-pressure utility line built to gas-transmission code, so 'transmission' is the closer of the three controlled-vocab options (never 'gathering' -- it does not collect from wellheads -- and never 'distribution' -- it serves industrial pump stations, not a local low-pressure customer network). resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM records LengthKnown=6.00 mi on P7820 (Phase I), but every source checked points to this being a value swapped with sibling row P7821 (Phase II), which currently records LengthKnown=0.00 mi. EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset is completely consistent on this across ALL 28 dated releases from 2018-05 through 2026-08: 'Atlantic Bridge project Phase 1' carries miles=0 (diameter and cost blank) in every single release, while 'Atlantic Bridge project Phase 2' carries miles=6.3, pipeline_diameter_inches=42, cost_millions=451.8 in every release from 2019-01 onward (Aug-2026 release: Phase 1 = Historical Projects (1996-2024) sheet, Excel row 871, miles=0; Phase 2 = same sheet, Excel row 1014, miles=6.3/diam=42/cost=451.8). This is not a one-off data artifact - it is a stable, repeated distinction EIA has drawn for seven years. It is corroborated operationally by Enbridge's own (2019) project page: 'The first phase of Atlantic Bridge, providing 40,000 dekatherms per day of incremental firm transportation service, began operating in November 2017. When the project facilities in New York are completed and placed into service, we will have full project capacity available from New Jersey to Massachusetts.' This explicitly states that Phase I went into service in Nov 2017 WITHOUT the New York pipe-replacement facilities being complete - i.e., Phase I's capacity was delivered without any new pipe, consistent with EIA's Phase-1 miles=0. The physical pipe scope in question - originally 18.1 mi across several replacement/loop segments in the 2015 pre-filing notice (FR Doc 2015-11409), narrowed by the 2016 EA (FR Doc 2016-10674) to 4.0 mi of 42-inch replacing 26-inch in Westchester County, NY plus 2.3 mi of 42-inch replacing 26-inch in Fairfield County, CT (= 6.3 mi total, matching EIA's Phase 2 figure exactly), alongside the new Weymouth compressor station in Norfolk County, MA - was completed later. Enbridge's 10-K (FY2020, SEC EDGAR accession 0000895728-21-000010) states the Weymouth compressor station was 'brought online' in January 2021, 'the third and final phase of Atlantic Bridge' reaching the full 133 mmcf/d - and P7821's OWN recorded StartYear1=2021/StartMonth1=1 already matches this exactly, while P7821's SegmentCost=451,800,000 USD already matches EIA's Phase 2 cost_millions=451.8 exactly. In other words: P7821 already carries the correct cost and start date for the phase that includes the 6.3 mi/42-inch pipe, but has LengthKnown=0 (wrong) where P7820 has LengthKnown=6.00 (also wrong) - a clean two-row value swap, not an isolated error. Filed as a cross_row_lead for P7821 as well. Diameter is correctly left blank on this row once Length=0, per the standing rule that an expansion with no new physical pipe carries Diameter=blank.
